note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.why:
Isaiah 61:1 says the Lord “hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted”. We are the brokenhearted. We are the ones crying out in the streets, to this day. And Job shows what the Lord does with us in that condition: “He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.”

The Lord is telling you there is going to be so much oppression going on that you are going to have to listen to the word of God. The Carmelo Anthony situation, that's oppression: he is in the prison house for defending himself. And the same week of his verdict, a baby was shot dead in Mississippi. These things are going to continue to happen.

Oppression, persecution, tribulation, all these things are going to arise for God's people to realize who they are. That is how he opens our ears. And yet some want to leave the truth because they got called fat, or because they got demoted. That is some evil stuff: traitors and betrayers.

So Isaiah 61 is proclaimed to the ones whose ears the oppression has opened: liberty to the captives, “the opening of the prison to them that are bound”, because we are yet this day in captivity and we fill the prison houses. What is there to hope for outside of the body of Christ? Only the ones who know who they are can look for “the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God”.

precepts.text: He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression. The oppressor is not poor; they are rich through robbery, and that continues to this day.
precepts.point: People say they hate camps, but the camps are the reason you understand the Bible the way you do. Your oppressor did not tell you that you were an Israelite; your own people did. God put the spirit on the men that came before us, the elders and those camps, and we got the fruits of that in our bishops today. The spirit continued to be carried out amongst us, a generation where we bethought ourselves and were brought back to our fathers. That is prophecy.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
Job 36:10 says the Lord “openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity”: he commanded, requested and called you to return from iniquity back to your heritage. Verse 15 shows where he opens those ears: “He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.”

The poor here are our people. It was through the oppression of the oppressor, and through the religion he gave us, that our ears were opened. Esau is not poor. They are rich through robbery, and that continues to this day. We are a people robbed and spoiled and hid in prison houses, as Isaiah 42 says, and it is being played out in real time.

Just because you are not in the prison system doesn't mean you are not in captivity. Deuteronomy 28:15-68 applies to us: the Lord gave us the warning, we didn't take heed, and the curses are in full effect. The 13th Amendment was supposed to end slavery, but its clause, except as punishment for crime, made the loophole that fills the prisons with our people for free labor. Slavery was never abolished; it evolved. They framed mischief and made it law, like the throne of iniquity that “frameth mischief by a law.” A warden speaks of a young man's sweat equity instead of the death penalty, the same spirit as the Willie Lynch letter: don't kill him, it's not good economics.

This is still the land of our captivity, and the enemy got crafty with us. But in that oppression the Lord opened our ears. We were deaf and now we hear discipline; we were blind and now we see. We are not supposed to be at rest in this land. Your 9-to-5 is not your purpose; your purpose is to keep his commandments, remember that you are called and requested of God, and magnify his law upon the earth.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.” When our people are oppressed, God opens their ears. All the things Trump is doing, and ICE is doing in the streets and in the black community, are God opening your ears. For the last 60 years our people have been lost and confused, following the American dream and thinking America is about equal rights and opportunity. God said, no, this place is not your rest. So he turns up the oppression, because that is the only time we as a people turn to God: when bad things start happening to us.

Hosea says it: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” Until we acknowledge our offence and seek God's face.

In our affliction we will seek him early: before it is too late, before we die, before judgment comes. So God is allowing Trump to do these things in the black community with these ICE agents so that you will seek him. Our people are realizing that the American dream is exactly what it is, a dream, and that there is no such thing here as justice and equal rights. That is why judgment starts first with the house of God.

precepts.text: When he slew them, then they sought him, and they returned and enquired early after God.
precepts.point: He delivereth the poor in his affliction and openeth their ears in oppression. Affliction is the only time the people turn to God.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
Psalm 78 shows the same pattern: “Therefore their days did he consume in vanity, and their years in trouble.” The trouble is affliction. “When he slew them, then they sought him: and they returned and enquired early after God.”

When God slew us. What do you see taking place all over the streets right now? Our people being oppressed, locked up, put in prison by ICE officers. Then we seek God. That is when we return and enquire early after the Lord: when bad things start happening to us.

That is why judgment must begin first at the house of the Lord. Number one, for us to turn back to our God. Number two, to prove us: as you turn to him, bad things will happen to see whether you believe and trust in him. “And they remembered that God was their rock, and the high God their redeemer.” He is the one who will redeem us from the condition we are in.

And Isaiah 30 gives the teachers their job: though the Lord gives the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, the teachers will not be removed into a corner any more. As our people cry under the affliction, we go to them and tell them why it is happening: this is the way, walk ye in it. Not guns, as some are calling for; the word of God is what will change our people and bring destruction on this place.

precepts.text: As a nation of people, if they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity.
precepts.point: For then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success: only after the mouth, the meditation, and the doing does prosperity follow. Thus saith God, the second you transgress the commandments of the Lord you cannot prosper, so any pastor teaching prosperity while saying the law is done away with is teaching a lie. Real prosperity never came from sowing a seed into a basket; it comes from obeying the laws of the Most High, and that applies to us as a whole nation of people.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“If they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.” As a nation of people, if they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity.

Real prosperity never came from sowing a seed into a basket; it comes from obeying the laws of the Most High, and that applies to us as a whole nation of people. Obey and serve him, and the days are spent in prosperity and the years in pleasures.

precepts.text: The Lord withdraws not his eyes from the righteous; if they be bound in cords of affliction, then he shows them their transgressions, opens their ear to discipline, and commands that they return from iniquity. If they obey they spend their days in prosperity; if not, they perish by the sword. Righteousness is not never sinning; it is being able to get back up, and if the Lord wants you, he will get you back right.
precepts.point: The Lord upholds David in his integrity and sets him before his face forever. The Lord kept him strong and moving in the right spirit.

note.label: Psalm 41: Blessed Is He That Considers the Poor

precepts.why:
“But thou, O Lord, be merciful unto me, and raise me up, that I may requite them.” Job shows how the Lord raises up a righteous man who has fallen: “He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings are they on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted. And if they be bound in fetters, and be holden in cords of affliction; Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded. He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity. If they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.” And if they do not obey, they perish by the sword.

Righteousness is not never sinning; it is being able to get back up. When the righteous are bound in cords of affliction, the Lord shows them their transgressions, opens their ear to discipline and commands them to return from iniquity. If the Lord wants you, he will get you back right.

That is how David knew the Lord favoured him: “mine enemy doth not triumph over me.” David went through much, including his own son trying to kill him and take the kingdom, but Absalom was not able to take the kingdom from him. The Lord upheld David in his integrity and set him before his face for ever; he kept him strong and moving in the right spirit, a king still on the throne.
